direct.label: Direct service connection letter
direct.basisDescription: the in-service event, injury, or exposure

interviewSlots.label: Diagnosis
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether a doctor has diagnosed this condition and what the doctor named it. If there is no diagnosis yet, that is fine to say.

interviewSlots.label: When symptoms started
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask when the symptoms first began and whether they have continued since service.

interviewSlots.label: In-service event
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask about the in-service event, injury, or exposure the condition is tied to, with a date or place if known.

interviewSlots.label: Treatment and records
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what treatment or records exist for this condition, such as service treatment records, VA care, or private care.

interviewSlots.label: What a provider has said
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether any doctor or provider has told the veteran this condition is connected to service, and what they said.

components.label: Records reviewed
components.guidance: Name, in general terms, the history and records reviewed (the Veteran's reported history, service treatment records, and current records). Do not invent records that were not provided.

components.label: Current diagnosis
components.guidance: State the current, diagnosed condition. Do not diagnose a condition that was not provided in the facts.

components.label: In-service event or injury
components.guidance: Describe the in-service event, injury, or exposure the Veteran reported, with any date or place provided.

components.label: Medical rationale
components.guidance: Explain, in plain clinical terms, why the current condition is consistent with that in-service event. This is the reasoning that supports the opinion.

components.label: Opinion statement
components.guidance: End the body with the at-least-as-likely-as-not opinion sentence, framed as the reviewing physician's opinion.

components.label: Signature block
components.guidance: Leave a signature block for the physician: name, credentials, license, date, and signature line. Leave these blank for the physician to complete.

interviewSlots.label: Diagnosis
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether a doctor has diagnosed this condition and what the doctor named it. If there is no diagnosis yet, that is fine to say.

interviewSlots.label: Service-connected condition
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask which condition the VA has already service-connected that is causing or worsening this one.

interviewSlots.label: When this started
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask when this condition began relative to the service-connected condition.

interviewSlots.label: Treatment and records
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what treatment or records exist for this condition, such as VA care or private care.

interviewSlots.label: What a provider has said
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether any doctor has told the veteran this condition was caused or worsened by the service-connected condition, and what they said.

components.label: Records reviewed
components.guidance: Name, in general terms, the history and records reviewed. Do not invent records that were not provided.

components.label: Current diagnosis
components.guidance: State the current, diagnosed claimed condition.

components.label: Primary service-connected condition
components.guidance: Name the condition the VA has already service connected that is said to have caused or worsened the claimed condition.

components.label: Medical rationale
components.guidance: Explain why the primary condition caused or aggravated the claimed condition. A separate in-service event is not required.

components.label: Opinion statement
components.guidance: End with the at-least-as-likely-as-not opinion sentence linking the claimed condition to the primary condition.

components.label: Signature block
components.guidance: Leave a signature block for the physician to complete. Leave the fields blank.

aggravation.label: Aggravation letter
aggravation.basisDescription: the worsening during service beyond natural progression

interviewSlots.label: Diagnosis
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether a doctor has diagnosed this condition and what the doctor named it.

interviewSlots.label: Before service
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what this condition was like before service, as the veteran remembers it.

interviewSlots.label: Worsening in service
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what happened during service that made it permanently worse beyond its normal course.

interviewSlots.label: Treatment and records
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what treatment or records exist for this condition from before, during, and after service.

interviewSlots.label: What a provider has said
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether any doctor has told the veteran that service permanently worsened this condition, and what they said.

components.label: Records reviewed
components.guidance: Name, in general terms, the history and records reviewed. Do not invent records that were not provided.

components.label: Current diagnosis
components.guidance: State the current, diagnosed condition.

components.label: Pre-service baseline
components.guidance: Describe what the condition was before service, as the Veteran reported it.

components.label: In-service worsening
components.guidance: Describe the specific duty, injury, or conditions of service that made it permanently worse beyond its natural progression.

components.label: Medical rationale
components.guidance: Explain why the in-service worsening exceeds the normal course of the condition.

components.label: Opinion statement
components.guidance: End with the at-least-as-likely-as-not opinion sentence framed in terms of aggravation.

components.label: Signature block
components.guidance: Leave a signature block for the physician to complete. Leave the fields blank.

supplemental.label: Supplemental or Board evidence letter
supplemental.basisDescription: the in-service event, injury, or exposure

interviewSlots.label: Diagnosis
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether a doctor has diagnosed this condition and what the doctor named it.

interviewSlots.label: Prior decision gap
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what the earlier VA decision said was missing, or why it denied the medical link.

interviewSlots.label: In-service event
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask about the in-service event, injury, or exposure the condition is tied to, with a date or place if known.

interviewSlots.label: Treatment and records
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask what treatment or records exist for this condition, including anything new since the prior decision.

interviewSlots.label: What a provider has said
interviewSlots.guidance: Ask whether any doctor has told the veteran this condition is connected to service, and what they said.

components.label: Records reviewed
components.guidance: Name, in general terms, the history and records reviewed. Do not invent records that were not provided.

components.label: What the prior decision was missing
components.guidance: Address why the earlier decision denied the medical link. New evidence must be new and relevant; do not repeat a letter the VA already has.

components.label: Current diagnosis
components.guidance: State the current, diagnosed condition.

components.label: In-service event or injury
components.guidance: Describe the in-service event, injury, or exposure the Veteran reported.

components.label: Medical rationale
components.guidance: Explain, with reasoning, why the current condition is related to service, filling the gap the prior decision identified.

components.label: Opinion statement
components.guidance: End with the at-least-as-likely-as-not opinion sentence.

components.label: Signature block
components.guidance: Leave a signature block for the physician to complete. Leave the fields blank.
